name: Hôtel des Grands Boulevards
description:
Hotel des Grands Boulevards is an Experimental Group property in Paris's 2nd arrondissement, set in a historic building reinterpreted by designer Dorothée Meilichzon.
The hotel has 50 bedrooms, a restaurant, and a rooftop terrace, with interiors that nod to Louis XVI romanticism without leaning on cliché.
Dining centres on the in-house restaurant and rooftop bar, both designed by Meilichzon as part of the building's full interior scheme.

images.description: A bright and airy lounge space features a prominent circular bar with a light marble countertop and a dark wood base adorned with a diamond pattern. The bar is surrounded by elegant wooden stools with red leather seats and topped with a black metal framework from which greenery and pendant lights hang. The space is illuminated by abundant natural light filtering through a large glass ceiling, offering glimpses of surrounding building facades. Several guests are visible seated at tables in the background, enjoying the sophisticated atmosphere.

The terrace is decorated with lush potted plants and climbing greenery, enclosed by a black metal railing. In the background, classic urban buildings with distinctive rooftops and chimneys are visible under a bright sky.

A potted tree stands in the foreground, with climbing plants on a dark trellis providing privacy. The space is well-maintained and offers an inviting outdoor seating area.
